subject: Request: Streaming vs Batch SLA - lead/initial latency waiver
messages:
From: Asha Gupta <asha@quantify.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming vs Batch SLA - request for differentiation

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — the team was impressed with Redwood’s latency profile. We’re finalizing internal requirements for the contract and have one sticking point: the streaming (server-push) endpoints behave differently from the synchronous endpoints we tested.

Quantify’s security and procurement teams are asking for explicit, separate commitments for streaming time-to-first-token (TTFT) and sustained token/sec expectations. Practically, we need a waiver or addendum that reflects:
- TTFT tolerance for streaming sessions (we observed ~450–800ms for initial tokens on long-context streams)
- sustained token/sec ranges for steady-state generation vs short bursts

Attached is a short proposal from our engineering team that proposes a 90-day pilot with modified TTFT commitments and an option to revisit at renewal (Quantify-SLA-diff-proposal.pdf). Can Redwood provide an exception path or a controlled carve-out in the SOW for streaming endpoints? Appreciate a short note on feasibility and any guardrails you’d want (timeouts, fallback to sync, penalty structures).

Best,
Asha
Procurement & Ops
Quantify.ai
Attachment: Quantify-SLA-diff-proposal.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Asha Gupta <asha@quantify.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming vs Batch SLA - request for differentiation

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear note and the attached proposal. Short answer: yes, we can support a scoped exception for streaming endpoints, but we need to define measurable boundaries and an operational plan. High-level proposal from our side: 

1) Metric definitions (explicit):
   - "lead-latency" (our term): time from request arrival to first token emitted for streaming endpoints.
   - "sustained throughput": median tokens/sec over a 60s sliding window during steady-state generation.

2) Proposed temporary commitments for pilot (90 days):
   - lead-latency (streaming): p95 <= 900ms for typical single-turn calls (seq len <= 1024). Note: we observed lower numbers in many cases but want to be conservative for the pilot.
   - lead-latency (sync/batched endpoints): p95 <= 250ms (unchanged from standard SLA).
   - sustained throughput: median range 120–400 tokens/sec for production prompts; allowed burst to 800 tokens/sec for short windows (<=10s) before soft-throttling.

3) Operational guardrails:
   - Fallback policy: when lead-latency exceeds threshold, route to compatible sync model variant (if client-level policy allows) and increment a per-minute fallback counter.
   - Monitoring & alerts: Redwood will expose route-level lead-latency metrics and a daily digest for Quantify to evaluate.
   - Credit/penalty: if streaming lead-latency p95 exceeds pilot threshold for more than 3 days in a 30-day window, we propose a credit formula (token-credit proportional to affected requests) defined in the SOW addendum.

4) Next steps:
   - If this looks acceptable, we’ll loop in Contracts and CS to draft a one-page addendum capturing the metric definitions, pilot duration, and credit formula.
   - Please confirm whether Quantify requires the thresholds for all regions or just us-region for the pilot.

I’ll copy our CS/Contracts folks once you confirm.

— Vivek
VP, GTM & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: contracts@redwood.com, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Streaming vs Batch SLA - request for differentiation

Folks — forwarding Quantify’s ask. Technical context below (copied from my notes):

> We observed initial token delays when the model backend is performing cross-request prefix merging + KV cache warmups on longer histories. This is more pronounced for streaming where the client expects immediate emission. For batch/sync calls we already amortize this at container scheduling and request coalescing.

A few points for the Contracts/Legal draft:
- Keep metric language prescriptive (define measurement windows, p95/p50, sample sets).
- Include explicit fallback behavior (we’re offering a route-to-sync fallback) and a cap on fallback counts to avoid infinite failover loops.
- We recommend the pilot be limited to US-region only to avoid multi-region variance during the initial 90 days.

Attachment suggestions for the addendum: redwood-sla-draft.docx (I’ll iterate on the credit math).

On the product side, Vivek — we can instrument a per-route lead-latency metric and a fallback counter in the next sprint; estimate 2 weeks to roll to staging. We should also lock the quantile (p95) definition and whether TTFT is calculated excluding cold-starts (I suggest excluding host cold-starts but including KV warmups).

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Product, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Asha Gupta <asha@quantify.ai>, procurements@quantify.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, contracts@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming vs Batch SLA - request for differentiation

Hi Asha — thanks for sending the proposal and Vivek/Karthik for the suggested pilot parameters. We’ve escalated this to Contracts and CS. Quick summary and action items: 

Summary of Redwood position (agreed internally):
- We will provision a 90-day streaming SLA addendum scoped to US-region traffic only.
- Lead-latency p95 bound for streaming endpoints: 900ms (pilot). Sync/batch endpoints remain at current SLA.
- Sustained throughput and burst bands as detailed by Vivek; we’ll capture measurement method and sample exclusion rules in the addendum.

Action items:
1) Contracts to draft one-page addendum (target draft by 2027-09-22). Attachment: redwood-sla-draft.docx.
2) Product (Karthik) to enable per-route lead-latency metric and fallback counter in staging (ETA 2 weeks).
3) CS (Monica) to run daily digests with Quantify during pilot and a weekly sync.

Asha — can you confirm whether Quantify is comfortable starting the pilot on 2027-10-01 and whether the pilot should include your Europe test cluster or remain US-only? Once we have your confirmation we’ll proceed with Contracts drafting and the DocuSign flow.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-sla-draft.docx
